subject: Post-demo: token efficiency roadmap & prioritized pilot asks
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@nebulacomm.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Anya Patel <anya.patel@nebulacomm.com>
Date: Sun, 19 May 2028 15:06:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up + priorities after today's demo

Tessa — thanks for the demo earlier. Quick recap from our side so we're all aligned and to surface the budget constraints we called out: 

Pain points we reiterated today:
- Per-token spend during peak hours is ballooning; forecasted run-rate would double our current ML infra line-item by Q4.
- Real-time latency requirement for the checkout assistant is <= 250ms P95 — so any batching that increases tail latency is risky.
- We have sensitive PII snippets in prompts; data residency and a clean audit trail matter for procurement.

Goals from vendor evaluation:
1) Reduce per-customer inference unit cost by 30–50% without breaking the latency target.
2) Validate a pilot that shows <10% quality drift for our top-20 intents.
3) Keep ops lift low — prefer hosted/dedicated with clear rollback.

Budget: procurement told us there is a pilot budget ceiling of $75k (3 months) unless we can show a 6–9 month ROI to justify more.

As discussed, your batching + KV caching + quantization levers sounded like the most likely path to get us there. Can you confirm the prioritized set of levers you propose for a small pilot, plus an initial ballpark for expected token reduction (range %)?

Thanks — happy to jump on a short follow-up.

— Liam
Head of AI Products
Nebula Commerce

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@nebulacomm.com>
Cc: Anya Patel <anya.patel@nebulacomm.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 May 2028 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up + priorities after today's demo

Liam — thanks for the clear recap and the budget/headline goals. Appreciate the constraints; I summarized the outcome and next steps below so we have a single source of truth.

Executive summary (what we propose for the pilot)
- Scope: 3-month pilot (staging -> limited production) covering checkout assistant: top-20 intents, session-based KV caching for repeated prompts, batching tuned by route to preserve 250ms P95, and a light quantization profile to shave token compute.
- Prioritized levers (order): 1) KV prefix caching (expected 15–30% token reduction on session repeat traffic), 2) Adaptive micro-batching (10–25% reduction when load allows, configured with strict latency SLO), 3) Mixed-precision/quantized model variant for background inference paths (5–15% additional cost reduction), 4) Response truncation + reranking for low-value generator tokens (small UX risk — we will A/B).
- Estimated token reduction: conservative case 22% (all combined conservatively), optimistic case up to 55% depending on repeat rate and tuning. We will produce a model for best / median / worst-case scenarios.

Attachments: I uploaded a lightweight scope and a first-pass TCO estimate (attached). The estimate assumes your current token profile and scales with three pilot throughput curves (low/medium/high).

Next steps (owner, due):
- Redwood: produce a pilot SOW + prioritized checklist and projected token-savings model — due Wed 5/22 (owner: me + Ben for econ numbers).
- Nebula: confirm the target traffic slice (example: 15% of checkout volume or specific geos) and share sample logs for token profiling — due Fri 5/24 (owner: Anya).
- Both: 30-minute alignment call to finalize SOW and agree rollback metrics — propose Tue 5/28 or Wed 5/29.

We can work to keep the pilot inside the $75k ceiling by staging rollout and focusing optimizations that don't require dedicated reserved capacity up front. If we can show a ~40% cost reduction in the pilot, we'd build the case for a dedicated commit to get better unit economics.

I'll leave Marissa and Ben on to scope implementation complexity and confirm the latency gating approach.

Thanks again — will follow up with the SOW and the rough token model on Wednesday.

— Tessa Morgan
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Schedule: calendly.com/tessa-redwood

Attachments: nebula-pilot-scope.xlsx; redwood-token-tco-estimate.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 May 2028 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up + priorities after today's demo

Looping in a couple quick engineering/ops checks based on the ask. TL;DR: pilot shape is feasible but we need two constraints nailed down from Nebula to size infra and latency gating cleanly.

Questions for Liam/Anya to answer before we finalize the SOW:
- Exact P95 latency target: is 250ms strict across all geos or only the primary US region? We can set regional fallbacks.
- Sample traffic distribution: % of repeat sessions vs one-off sessions (this materially affects KV cache ROI).
- Which intents are mission-critical (list of top 20 ok) and which can tolerate small quality regressions for a short period?

From an ops perspective: micro-batching works well if we can tolerate a 5–15ms additional scheduler overhead in the median; the real danger is tail. We'll instrument with a strict SLO and a circuit-breaker that falls back to single-request routing if P95 creeps.

Ben — can you take the attached token file and produce a quick sensitivity table for the conservative / median / optimistic curves? Tessa, if Ben can get this by EOD Wed we can include it in the SOW.

— Marissa
Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@nebulacomm.com>
Cc: Anya Patel <anya.patel@nebulacomm.com>
Date: Thu, 23 May 2028 10:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up + priorities after today's demo

Hi all — ran a quick sensitivity on the token profile you shared (thanks Anya). High level numbers below (conservative / median / optimistic) for combined levers (KV caching + micro-batching + light quantization):

- Conservative: 18% token reduction -> estimated pilot spend reduction ~22% (because of fixed infra overheads).
- Median: 36% token reduction -> estimated pilot spend reduction ~38%.
- Optimistic: 52% token reduction -> estimated pilot spend reduction ~50–55% (if repeat session rate > 35% and we use dedicated reserved instances mid-pilot).

Notes and clarifications:
- These figures assume strict latency SLO gating (we throttle batching windows to maintain 250ms P95). If Nebula is willing to loosen P95 to 300ms in non-critical geos, median/optimistic improve noticeably.
- For the $75k pilot cap, we can run a 3-month test at Nebula's proposed 15% traffic slice with a median-savings plan and still show a 6-month payback at mid-volume growth (assuming stabilization of repeat rates).
- I'll produce the sensitivity table and include a short appendix on risk triggers (quality drift, tail latency) for your SOW.

Next actions:
- Redwood (Ben/Tessa): finalize numeric sensitivity table + SOW doc by EOD Fri 5/24.
- Nebula (Anya): send sample tokenized logs and top-20 intent list by Fri 5/24.
- Both: alignment call Tue 5/28 at 11:00am PT (meeting invite forthcoming).

Liam — happy to jump on a call to walk these scenarios live if helpful.

— Ben Carter
Principal Economist | Redwood Inference
